Red Hat Enterprise Linux System Administration I
This chapter shows how to manage and watch a server from a browser with Web Console. You learn where Red Hat help lives and how to ask for it.
You also learn how Red Hat Insights finds known problems and how to fix them.
Topics in this chapter, in book order:
Getting Help from Red Hat Customer Portal
Detecting and Resolving Issues with Red Hat Insights
Web Console is a web page that lets you manage and watch a server from a browser.
is a web-based management tool for Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8. It is built on the open source
service. You can read system logs and see graphs of performance. You can also change settings with graphical tools, and even open a full interactive terminal.
Think of it as a car dashboard for your server. Gauges and switches sit in one place. A dashboard cannot do everything, so the built-in terminal covers the rest.

Getting Help from Red Hat Customer Portal
The Customer Portal is Red Hat's support website, and Knowledgebase is its library of solutions.
) gives you documentation, downloads, tools and expert help.
holds solutions, FAQs and articles you can search. You can also submit and manage support tickets, manage subscriptions and get software updates and evaluations.
Some parts are open to everyone. Other parts need an active
(a paid right to Red Hat software and support). Think of a library with a public reading room and a members-only floor. Help with access is at

Detecting and Resolving Issues with Red Hat Insights
Insights is a cloud service that warns you about problems before they hurt your servers.
means using data to forecast trouble. Insights does this for security, performance, availability and stability. It is
(software as a service): it runs in Red Hat's cloud, so you need no extra servers, and you get new recommendations at once.
Red Hat keeps adding rules, based on common support risks, security flaws and known-bad settings. For each issue, Insights gives a risk estimate and a fix. The fix may be an
(an automation script) or plain steps. Think of a smoke alarm that also tells you which wire is faulty.
The product is Red Hat Insights, found on the Customer Portal. It supports RHEL 6.4 and later, Red Hat Virtualization 4, OpenShift Container Platform and Cloud Suite.
Red Hat's current documentation calls the service Red Hat Lightspeed, with its console at https://console.redhat.com/insights/. The

3.5 The tabs of the Insights interface
The Insights interface is split into tabs, and each tab has one job.

Reports show the state of a system over time. You get a risk score for all systems, recommended actions by category and severity, the last check-in time of each system, and the issues to fix first. Each tab answers a different question, so you move between them as you work. Think of the tabs in a filing cabinet.
A dashboard. Newest Systems, an Actions Summary (Low, Medium, High, Critical), a Plan Summary and new rules from the last 15 days.
Details of recommended actions. An Issues chart splits them into Availability, Stability, Performance and Security. A Risk summary graph groups them by risk.
All registered systems, with filters. Last Check In shows the latest update. Status shows the pending actions.
Maintenance plans. Pick issues for systems, choose how to handle them, and make an Ansible Playbook.
All rules, filtered by age, total risk, category, likelihood and impact. An Ansible logo means a playbook exists.
An overall score from historical data. You can export it as a PDF.
Settings for the service, for example a weekly email summary.
You must have at least 10 systems registered with Red Hat Insights for the Executive Report to be generated.
The tabs are Overview, Actions, Inventory, Planner, Rules, Executive Report and Configuration.

3.6 Viewing issues reported by Red Hat Insights
Move from the Overview down to one system to see its issues.

Log in and open the Insights page. On the Overview tab, look at Newest Systems and the Actions Summary percentages. On the Actions tab, click a graph for details about security, stability or critical issues. On the Inventory tab, see all systems. Click one system to list every issue that affects it.
Think of zooming from a city map down to a single street.
